content.text:
I fixed `parse_date` in `dates/parse.py`, and all 3 tests in `tests/test_parse.py` now pass, including `test_dates`.

The function now accepts a trailing `Z` and returns a timezone-aware UTC datetime. Input without `Z` still returns a naive datetime, so `test_naive` and `test_day_key` are unaffected.

A `Z` timestamp now returns an aware datetime where it used to raise. If any caller compares those values with naive ones, Python will raise a `TypeError`. I didn't check callers outside the tests.
